steps.text: Preheat the oven to 325 degrees F (160 degrees C).
Sprinkle both sides of brisket with salt, pepper, and garlic powder. Place in a Dutch oven or large roasting pan with a cover.
Cook in the preheated oven, covered, without adding water, for 3 hours.
Remove brisket from the pan and slice. Return slices to pan. Mix BBQ sauce with water; pour over sliced brisket. Cover the pan and cook for 1 more hour.

raw_recipe.headline: Oven BBQ Beef Brisket
raw_recipe.description: This BBQ brisket is cooked slowly in the oven, sliced, and then coated with BBQ sauce and braised until tender, delicious, and full of flavor.

review.reviewBody:
This recipe renders a fork-tender, juicy and flavorful brisket. As others have suggested, I substituted a cup of beer for the water. 
One (perhaps obvious) note; before slicing the brisket, let it rest for 10-15 minutes to allow the juices to re-distribute.

The celebration was my father-in-law's 90th birthday party! Used this recipe as our starting point. Talked with the butcher and he convinced me to buy an untrimmed brisket. He said cooking it with the fat added a great deal of flavor. So for 20 guests I bought a 13 pound untrimmed brisket. Based on this recipe and recommendations. we cooked ours in the oven 7 hours at 275 degrees. This was the perfect amount of time. Took it out and trimmed all the fat off, and then sliced as thin as we could. While cooking, used some rub on the meat as suggested and nearly a can of beer. We cooked it the day before. Also made Big Al's BBQ Sauce on this site. After cooking and slicing, soaked it all night long in the sauce and then warmed slowly on 275 degrees before the party. It was fabulous! Everyone raved. Served on nice rolls with some good deli cheddar cheese. Yummy.

Super simple and delicious. Reviewers who say it's too fatty should be aware that with Brisket, most recipes tell you to remove as much of the thick fat layer as you can before cooking. This recipe unfortunately doesn't tell you that, but it's almost always a good idea. The only other changes I made to this recipe were 1) I put a thin layer of barbecue sauce on the meat for the first round of cooking, then more in the second (after slicing), and 2) I split the cooking time approximately in half, rather than just leaving an hour of cooking after slicing the meat .

Incidentally, reviewers who say their meat turned out (or usually turns out) like shoe leather should be careful about which cuts of meat they use for slow cooking like this. You need a fatty, gristly cut like brisket because the collagen (in the gristle) breaks down slowly and tenderizes the meat. Leaner, finer cuts like steaks don't have much gristle and are much better for grilling, searing, frying, etc.

I did make two adjustments after reading reviews and my own personal experience with red meat. I did not salt before cooking, that usually draws out the moisture. Secondly, I used one cup beer instead of water. Was very good for my first brisket! Was a bit dry but very tender. Will try not slicing it next time around until right before serving to see if that helps! Usually best to wait 5-10 minutes after taking from oven to slice for max. juiciness. Family loved it, no left overs!

PLEASE READ - I added smoked paprika. I didn't measure the seasonings because the amount of seasonings is based on the size of the brisket. Just use enough to lightly coat both sides of the brisket. Use a pan that has a lip around the entire pan. That's important to get a good seal with your aluminum foil. Bake fat side down. The fat almost disappears during the cooking cycle. One hour before it's done I drained the liquid created by the brisket, sliced it then added the 1 cup of water/1 cup of your favorite barbecue sauce (mixed) to the pan, resealed and returned to the oven for the remaining hour. THE BRISKET WAS THE BEST I'VE EVER HAD! THE FLAVOR WAS OUT OF THIS WORLD AND IT WAS MELT IN YOUR MOUTH TENDER!! YOU MUST TRY THIS SIMPLE RECIPE

The brisket I used was just over 2.5 pounds. I seasoned following the recipe but I think a BBQ rub would be good too flavor profile . I did add 1/4 cup beef broth and put the brisket in a cast iron Dutch oven fat side up (important). At 3 hours I removed from the oven and let sit for about 20 minutes before cutting off the thickest fat and slicing… it was very tender. Since it was a smaller brisket, I mixed 2/3 cup each BBQ sauce and beef broth, poured over the slices and returned to oven for about an hour. Good cooking method - you can change up flavor profile with different spices and the style of BBQ sauce.

This is the best and easiest brisket that I have ever done. It is so tender. 5# is perfect size for my family. I didn’t have a Dutch oven with a lid that I could put in the oven but Turkey size oven bag works great !!
This turned out great. The only suggestion I would make is to line the pan you bake the brisket in with foil or parchment paper. Clean up can be a chore.

This recipe is absolutely amazing. The biggest complain I've run into is that the meat is dry and/or the meat is too tough or chewy. I've made this twice now and the meat comes out perfect. One tip I could add is to make sure the brisket is sealed up tight in the foil. Also, instead of using water, I used the dripping from the brisket and mixed that with the BBQ sauce. It turns out great that way and tastes amazing.

This was quite tasty and didn't require too much attention. The ONLY change that I will make next time is to add liquid smoke to it. That was missed, but otherwise it was good and I will make it again.

this was by far the best oven brisket I've tried yet,however I incorporated a couple ingredients instead of water beef stock, as far as dry seasons added brown sugar and tony thactherys Cajun season and olive oil.take brisket and wipe dry cover lightly in olive oil,take dry season mixed together in equal amounts and rub in.put in frig for six hours or better.when it's cooked you will find it fork tender with lots of flavor,enjoy all you great cooks
Easy to make and great taste.
I have been making this recipe for many years. It never disappoints. Serve it with beans and coleslaw.
Absolutely delicious
This was so easy! Very hands off and makes the house smell wonderful while it’s cooking. It’s not as tender as smoked brisket, but still really good.
Very easy, tender and delicious! Will definitely make it again
Easy to do. Brisket is moist and flavorful. A family favorite.
Amazing. Close to my favorite barbeque restaurant in Kansas City.
I’ve tried many recipes for brisket in the oven, and this is the BEST, without a doubt.
It was easy and came out great , I would certainly make it again!
